title: Shortest String That Contains Three Strings
summary: Given three strings a, b, and c, determine the shortest string that includes all three as substrings.
statement: Given three strings a, b, and c, determine the shortest string that includes all three as substrings. If multiple solutions exist, provide the lexicographically smallest one. Return the resulting string. Note that a string a is lexicographically smaller than string b if, at the first differing position, a has a character that precedes b in the alphabet. A substring is a continuous segment of characters within a string.
constraints: Return a string containing a, b, and c as substrings.
First minimize result length; among tied shortest results choose the lexicographically smallest.
Input strings may already contain one another.
hints: Try all six input orders because only three strings exist.
Merge an ordered pair using the largest suffix-prefix overlap, first discarding a contained string.
Build each ordered candidate and minimize by (length,text).
Any shortest superstring induces an occurrence order; maximal overlaps minimize that order, and enumerating all orders plus lexicographic comparison finds the required optimum.
editorial: Any shortest superstring induces an occurrence order; maximal overlaps minimize that order, and enumerating all orders plus lexicographic comparison finds the required optimum.

tests.explanation: Merging aaa before bca gives aaabca, the shortest lexicographically smallest result.
Only ab and ba need joining; aba is the shortest result.
